findings.title: Closing one strategy shuts down the factory's shared pool, so messages after a rebalance are silently skipped
findings.description:
`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`, `terminate()`, and `join()` all call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (lines 335-342), which stops every worker and shuts down every queue. The pool is owned by the factory (`result_consumer.py:102`, created at 131-137). `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` passes that same pool to every strategy it builds (`result_consumer.py:247-255`). The only reset is `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown()` (`result_consumer.py:183-185`).

Arroyo's StreamProcessor closes the strategy on partition revoke and calls `create_with_partitions` again on the same factory. This is from arroyo's lifecycle contract, not something I could read here, so confirm it against `sentry-arroyo>=2.28.0`. If that holds, the next strategy's `submit` runs `FixedQueuePool.submit`. That adds the offset (line 211), then `put` raises `queue.ShutDown` (stdlib `queue.py:151-152`). `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches the error (317-325), marks the offset complete, and the commit thread then commits past it (line 287 plus `result_consumer.py:251`). Every message after the first rebalance is logged as an error and committed unprocessed.

The batched-parallel mode shares `parallel_executor` across strategies and shuts it down only in the factory (`result_consumer.py:121`, 181-182). The new code lets a strategy's lifecycle destroy a factory-owned resource. No test closes a strategy and then creates a second one from the same factory.

Fix: give each strategy its own pool, created in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` and shut down in that strategy's `close()`. Or have `close()` only drain its own work. Add a test that closes one strategy, builds another from the same factory, and checks that the second processes and commits correctly.

findings.title: Enqueue failures are recorded as completed offsets
findings.description:
`FixedQueuePool.submit` records the offset as outstanding (line 211) before `put` (line 212). Any exception from `put` reaches the blanket `except Exception` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` (line 317). That handler logs the error and then calls `add_offset` and `complete_offset` (lines 319-325). The message is never processed, but the offset is marked done and the commit thread can advance past it.

This is the mechanism behind the FAIL above and would also drop data on any future enqueue error. Enqueue before recording the offset, and on enqueue failure re-raise or stop the processor. Keep the skip-and-complete path only for decode and grouping failures, which are meant to be skipped.

findings.title: Shutdown abandons queued work even though the queues are shut down to drain it
findings.description:
`FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` (lines 233-234) before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` (line 238). `OrderedQueueWorker.run` checks that flag at the top of each loop (line 129), so each worker exits after its current item and never reaches the drain. Stdlib `get()` would have returned the remaining items (`queue.py:192-193`).

Queued items are never processed or committed, so they are redelivered after restart. At-least-once still holds. But the docstring promise "No item is lost" (line 252) and the "Gracefully shutdown" comment (line 232) overstate this. `test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown` (`test_results_consumer.py:1987-2005`) does not check how many items were processed, so it cannot detect this.

Fix: remove the flag check and let `ShutDown` end the loop, or document abandon semantics and bound the wait on in-flight work.

findings.title: Work queues are unbounded, so the advertised backpressure never happens
findings.description:
Each queue is `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (line 185). Stdlib's default of 0 means unbounded (`queue.py:153`). Each `WorkItem` keeps the full Kafka `Message` alive (line 31). If processing is slower than consumption, queued items and their payloads grow without limit. `poll()` (lines 327-333) only emits a gauge, so nothing throttles `submit`. The class docstring (line 253) promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up," which cannot happen. A stuck worker also keeps its offsets outstanding, so `all_offsets` grows without bound.

Fix: pass a `maxsize`. A blocking `put` gives real backpressure, and `put` raises `ShutDown` on shutdown (`queue.py:160-161`), so existing handling still applies. Or remove the claim.

findings.title: Docstring promises commits only after successful processing, but failures are committed too
findings.description:
`OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches every exception from `result_processor` (lines 144-147), then completes the offset in `finally` (lines 148-149). A failed item is therefore committed like a successful one. That matches the existing modes, since `ResultProcessor.__call__` swallows exceptions (`result_consumer.py:44-54`), so the behavior is probably the right one. The docstring is still wrong, and the test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` assumes the intended behavior.

Fix: correct the docstring to say failed results are logged and committed.

findings.title: Offsets are committed from a background thread through arroyo's Commit callable
findings.description: `_commit_loop` calls `self.commit_function` from a thread the processor does not own. That function is arroyo's `Commit`, wrapped at `result_consumer.py:249-252`. The arroyo consumer is normally driven from the processor thread. I could not read arroyo in this sandbox, so I cannot confirm the `Commit` callable is safe to call concurrently with the consumer's poll and commit path. Verify this. If it is not safe, move the commit into `poll()` or `submit()` on the processor thread. That also removes the extra thread.

findings.title: Gap handling blocks commits for one pass, then skips the gap on the next
findings.description:
`start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)` (line 86) re-anchors at the lowest tracked offset after `mark_committed` drops everything at or below the committed offset (line 105). Trace it: offsets 100, 102, and 103 complete, and 101 never arrives. Pass 1 commits 100 and stops at the gap (line 92). Pass 2 starts at min=102 and commits 103.

A hole is not a record in Kafka, so skipping it is probably right. But the docstrings and tests say gaps "prevent committing past the gap" (`test_queue_consumer.py:352`, `test_results_consumer.py:1926-1983`). Decide on one contract and make the code and tests match it.

findings.title: Two uptime tests assert the wrong thing and cannot detect the bugs they name
findings.description:
- `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` (line 1874) says errors do not block commits. Line 1922 asserts that no commit happened for the partition. The poll loop breaks about 0.2s after processing (lines 1962-1968), before the 1-second commit pass (`queue_consumer.py:273-277`). The assertion passes whether or not errors block commits. It should wait for a commit and assert 102, since the failed message at 100 is completed in `finally`.
- `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps` (line 1926) asserts that every commit is at most 101 (lines 1979-1983). The loop stops about 1.3s in, before the second pass at about 2s. That pass would commit 104, because after committing 100 the tracker holds {102, 103}. The test passes only because of timing.

findings.title: The Kafka offset-commit test samples a fixed 5-second window and can flake
findings.description:
The test calls `processor._run_once()` for a fixed 5 seconds (line 2102) and then asserts on what was committed. That window must cover consumer-group join, the first fetch, and the strategy's 1-second commit pass. Kafka's default initial rebalance delay for a new group is about 3 seconds, which leaves little margin. The test never polls for the expected committed offset of 5.

It also calls the private `_run_once` and `_shutdown` methods, calls `factory.shutdown()` outside a `finally`, and swallows cleanup errors (lines 2145-2146). `KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES` (line 2062) has no effect, because `StreamProcessor` receives `Topic(test_topic)` directly.

Fix: poll until the committed offset reaches 5 with a deadline, and wrap the lifecycle in `try`/`finally`.

findings.title: Thread-queue tests never close their strategies, and the shutdown test runs unmocked processing
findings.description:
- `test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown` does not mock `result_processor.__call__`, unlike the other tests. Five real `ResultProcessor` calls run on worker threads. `get_from_cache` (`src/sentry/db/models/manager/base.py:283`) queries the database on a cache miss, and that query runs on another thread outside the test's transaction. The test asserts only that `factory.queue_pool is None` (line 2005).
- No thread-queue test calls `strategy.close()`. Each strategy's `_commit_loop` (`queue_consumer.py:273`) keeps running for the rest of the session and calls the test's commit closures every second.

Fix: close each strategy in `tearDown` or a `finally`, and mock the processor or assert on processed items in the shutdown test.

findings.title: Several assertions depend on timing or on hash seeds
findings.description: `assert stats["total_items"] > 0` (line 200) runs right after submitting 10 items. `total_items` counts only items still queued, so it can be 0 if workers have already picked them up. `test_different_groups_distributed` (line 106) depends on `hash(str)` distribution, which is salted per process. With 20 keys over 3 queues, a bucket is missed roughly 0.1% of the time. Tests named "concurrent" (`test_queue_consumer.py:137` and `:314`, and `test_results_consumer.py:1780`) only assert call counts and never check concurrency.

findings.title: Dead code and duplicated skip logic
findings.description: `wait_until_empty` (lines 222-229) has no callers in `src` or `tests`. `WorkItem.message` (line 31) is set in `submit` (line 312) but never read, yet it keeps every Kafka message alive while queued. The `except queue.ShutDown` inside the processing `try` (lines 142-143) cannot trigger, because `result_processor` catches everything. The skip-and-complete block is duplicated at lines 302-303 and 320-325, and a helper would remove the duplication.

findings.title: Hash comment and mode help text are inaccurate
findings.description: `get_queue_for_group` describes itself as "consistent hashing", but `hash(group_key) % num_queues` is modulo hashing on a per-process salted string hash. Ordering only needs stability within one process, which holds, but the docstring should say so. Separately, `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:123` still says "Parallel uses multithreading." That predates this change, and the "parallel" mode actually uses multiprocessing (`result_consumer.py:126-130`). The help text also does not describe the new mode.

findings.title: New mode is wired consistently and the required APIs exist on the pinned Python
findings.description: The CLI choice (`src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:121`) matches the `Literal` on the factory (`result_consumer.py:108`) and the dispatch in `create_with_partitions`. The pinned runtime is Python 3.13.1, so `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` exist (`queue.py:36`, `:233`). The commit path adds +1 to the offset (`result_consumer.py:251`), which matches Kafka's next-offset semantics. The test helper imports resolve: `requires_kafka` (`src/sentry/testutils/skips.py:54`), `create_topics` and `wait_for_topics` (`batching_kafka_consumer.py:12`, `:46`), and `get_kafka_admin_cluster_options` (`kafka_config.py:92`, which takes the extra options as its second argument).
